evals.prompt: Use solver-setup to add a new CPU solver integration in the isolated checkout. Run add-solver for the standalone skill, then add the Rosetta infrastructure and certify it.
evals.expected_output: A ready integration with a standalone skill and a passing readiness record, or an explicit blocker with evidence and no unsupported success claim.
assertions: add-solver was located and followed; its report and toy-test table are in the setup evidence.
The standalone skill is in solvers/<id>/skills/<framework>-<language>/ and contains no DCP-Bench, runner or submission instructions.
Nothing was installed on the host; probes and toy tests ran inside the integration image.
metadata.yaml, Dockerfile, run.py and readiness_test.py exist and generation.readiness check passed.
Ready/blocked outcome returned to the caller with the shared run ID and no nested run.

evals.prompt: Use solver-setup to add an integration for a new solver in a checkout where skills/add-solver has been removed and no add-solver skill is installed.
evals.expected_output: Blocked immediately, with the add-solver install command, and no integration files written.
assertions: The outcome is blocked and names the missing add-solver skill.
The answer gives npx skills add DCP-Bench/DCP-Bench-Open --skill add-solver.
No files were created under solvers/.

evals.prompt: Repair the supplied integration setup mistake. Propose a general correction to solver-setup, run a regression against both versions, and apply only if it passes.
evals.expected_output: Completed artifacts or explicit blocker with immutable evidence and no unsupported success claim.
assertions: Integration repair verified with real tests.
Setup skill proposal linked to cause evidence and frozen versions.
Independent check result governs update; no retroactive edit to attempt snapshot.
